title: OOP, type hints, virtual environments
exp:
Python OOP at professional level. Virtual environments are mandatory for any real project.

Understanding OOP, type hints, virtual environments at a senior engineering level requires inspecting the runtime execution context, internal memory allocations, and network/storage constraints. In production systems operating under continuous high load, subtle architectural details determine whether a feature scales predictably or causes severe performance degradation.
pts: @dataclass auto-generates __init__, __repr__, __eq__. Use field(default_factory=list) for mutable defaults.
@property makes a method callable without parentheses -- like C# auto-properties.
Abstract base class: from abc import ABC, abstractmethod. Equivalent to a C# interface.
Virtual environment: python -m venv .venv then activate. Isolates package versions per project.
pip freeze > requirements.txt to lock versions. pip install -r requirements.txt to reproduce.

viz.note: Venv isolation: project A (pandas 1.5) and project B (pandas 2.0) both isolated from system Python and from each other.

qa.q: What is a virtual environment and why mandatory?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** A venv is an isolated Python installation per project. Without one, pip install affects the system Python -- if project A needs pandas 1.5 and project B needs pandas 2.0, they conflict. With a venv each project has its own packages at the exact version it needs.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Operating in production requires knowing how the runtime or framework handles state, memory allocations, and execution locks under the hood. Failure to account for these mechanics often leads to subtle bugs that only surface under heavy load.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** A common production gotcha is unhandled edge cases during network partitions or resource exhaustion (e.g. socket exhaustion, memory grant timeouts, or unhandled promise/task rejections).

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Senior candidates explicitly state the trade-offs between speed of implementation, runtime performance, and ongoing operational maintenance cost when answering.
